chapter: Louisville, Buck and the carnival years
title: Humboldt Collins introducing the boys at white parties
summary: Collins' provocative introduction won over white hosts, and Bubbles praises the Judge again for getting him on the road.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Why? Why --you've got the question of why and I told you why. About the Detention Home situation, how much I appreciate the Judge making the decision he made because he knew later on in life I was going to do more harm than what I did. And that's only the beginning -- and at my age, what am I going to do with somebody that hangs out with me that's older than me, that hangs out with me. See what I mean? So I give the Judge credit for using the judgment he used by letting my mother take me out of the school, take me out of town to get me out of the Detention Home. I thought that was beautiful. He doesn't know what a favor he did for me. You understand? Because I was traveling ever since. Ever since. Now, I go with this carnival -- not the circus now -- I went with the carnival. So I went with the carnival for about -- I'd been playing partners and everything, Buck and I playing the barrooms ane everything, I told you that; and this guy Humbolt Collins used to take us around and he had a

way of introducing us that was superior. Superior. He would go to your house or any friend's house who were white, ring the bell and his entrance was, "let us niggers in and if you don't want us niggers here we'll leave." They liked him so well that they over- looked that we were colored. They received him and Buck and I as though we were one of them. If we entertained, we were four times greater.
Who was this person that was introducing you?

No, he was just a fella that had the Indiana Trucks I told ya. He took it upon himself to take us around to different parties. He wanted them to hear us entertain. You understand? And through him was a great movement because his saying nigger didn't mean nothing, 'cause we knew he was white, we knew he was white. What he was saying didn't mean nothing. You understand? What meant something was him telling this other white fella who he had that the word when he used it wasn't as harmful to us as it would be

to George and Jim. You get my point? Therefore, they received us knowing that we know who we are without them saying who we were. And they don't have to bring up the term at all, 'cause he's already introduced us as being one of us -- us -- he used the term, it was us.
